intended_object: The Euclidean radius R = (1 - |a|^2)/(2|Im(conj u · a)|) of the circle orthogonal to the unit circle that carries the hyperbolic geodesic through a in the unit disc with unit direction u (when that geodesic misses the origin). Inferred from the docstring and the module on Poincaré-disc orthogonal circles.
explanation: Independent derivation with |u| = 1: the centre is c = a + i t u for real t, with radius R = |t|. Orthogonality to the unit circle means |c|^2 = 1 + R^2, so |a|^2 + 2t·Re(i·conj(a)·u) = 1. Since Re(i·conj(a)·u) = Im(conj(u)·a), this gives R = (1 - |a|^2)/(2|Im(conj u · a)|), which is exactly the body. The docstring is explicit that outside the hypotheses |u| = 1, |a| < 1, A ≠ 0 the value is only an algebraic parameter (0 at A = 0 by the division-by-zero convention, negative for |a| > 1, e.g. -3/4 at u = 1, a = 2i, which checks out). Those values are junk outside the natural domain. The construction belongs to the Poincaré disc model in ℂ, so ℂ is its natural setting, and Mathlib has no corresponding definition.
